doc.title: Steve Buckingham, interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, February 25, 2019 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Meeting George Massenburg and deciding to become a studio guitarist
summary: On a Baltimore recording trip engineer George Massenburg invited him to watch a mix; seeing studio musicians arrive made him decide to be a session guitarist.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: of Richmond on Monday morning. So everybody went back but me. He said, “Do you want to stay over and watch me mix tomorrow? Monday morning. I said yeah. So I stayed over, go to the studio on Monday morning and we’re in one studio, in Baltimore and this was of course four track recording. And in another studio across the hall I saw these guys walking in with guitar cases and stuff, I said, “Who are they?” He said, “They’re studio musicians.” He said they’re here to play on somebody’s record or a jingle or something like that. And like the light bulb goes off. I took the bus home from Baltimore to Richmond with the tape. I told my parents I wanted to become a studio guitar player. And they said just finish college and you can do whatever you want. And I did. But I started playing in sessions while I was still in college.
